result.lens:
NEWS, ANNOUNCEMENTS AND SURPRISE.

The central distinction: every one of the 735 dead tests used the LEVEL or CHANGE of a macro series indexed by its as-of date and shifted by PUB_LAG. That object is "the data." It is not "the news." The news content of a release is (actual first print − what was expected), and none of the 735 features contain an expectation term at all. A second, entirely untouched object is the RELEASE CALENDAR ITSELF — which is knowable months in advance, carries zero lookahead risk, and says nothing about any macro value. A third is REVISIONS, which are published data the market demonstrably underweights relative to headlines. All three are orthogonal to what has been tested.

What is genuinely free for expectations (verified reasoning about sources, not assumed):
- ALFRED / FRED vintages (`series/observations` with realtime_start/realtime_end, output_type=2). Free API key, instant registration, no cost tier. Gives every first print, every subsequent revision, and the exact date each value entered FRED. This is the workhorse: it lets you build a REAL-TIME statistical expectation (nothing but pre-release vintages in the information set) and therefore a surprise, for every series already on disk.
- FRED `release/dates` endpoint: official release dates for every series, free. Removes all PUB_LAG guesswork for release-day event studies.
- Atlanta Fed GDPNow historical vintages (xlsx, no key) and Philadelphia Fed ADS Business Conditions Index vintages (xlsx, no key). These are professionally-built nowcasts whose vintage-to-vintage REVISION is, by construction, the news content of whatever released that day, already aggregated and denominated in growth units.
- Cleveland Fed inflation nowcasting. Published pre-release CPI/PCE nowcast — the closest thing to a genuinely free consensus for the highest-attention release. Current values are certainly free; the full historical vintage archive should be confirmed before relying on it, so I treat it as a cross-check on the ALFRED-built CPI expectation rather than a load-bearing input.
- BIS Central bankers' speeches dataset and the Federal Reserve's own speech listing: dated, attributed, full text, free.

What I am REJECTING as not genuinely free or not viable, despite being in the brief:
- Bloomberg / Reuters / Econoday consensus: paid. Investing.com and TradingEconomics historical forecast columns are scrapeable but are TOS-gray, silently backfilled, and unversioned — I would not build a strategy on them and would not trust a backtest that used them.
- Sovereign credit-rating actions on the US: n = 3 in the entire modern era (S&P 2011, Fitch 2023, Moody's 2025). There is no statistical test to run. For a broader sovereign panel there is no free, clean, machine-readable action history with timestamps. Rejected outright.
- GPR (Caldara-Iacoviello) and EPU (Baker-Bloom-Davis) geopolitical/uncertainty indices: free and daily, but they are newspaper-count LEVELS, i.e. exactly the class of object that 735 tests just killed, and both are documented as explaining contemporaneously rather than predicting. Proposing them would be a restatement in a new costume. Rejected.
- Any sub-daily release-timing structure (08:30 ET drop vs the equity open, first-30-minute reversal): the repo has daily OHLC only, and intraday timeframes plus session drifts are already declared dead. Not testable here; not proposed.

Power discipline that shaped the six below: at 652 weekly obs a t=3 needs ~0.85 annualized Sharpe; at 150 monthly obs it needs the same annualized Sharpe but with far uglier estimator variance. So I have deliberately weighted the proposals toward WEEKLY-native surprises (initial claims is the only tier-1 US release at weekly frequency) and toward one conditioning test on the existing MNQ survivor, where the bar is an interaction coefficient rather than a standalone edge that must clear FDR from scratch. Each hypothesis should be pre-registered with ONE primary test and one asset, with everything else marked as secondary, or the FDR burden will eat all of them.

hypotheses.name: Real-time release surprise composite (claims-backboned, ALFRED vintages)
hypotheses.claim: The standardized surprise of a macro release — first print minus a strictly real-time statistical expectation built only from pre-release vintages — predicts the sign of 1-day and 5-day returns in XAUUSD and MNQ, whereas the same series' level or change (already tested, already dead) does not. Primary pre-registered test: weekly initial-claims surprise z-score, negated, predicting MNQ 5-day return from the close of the day after the release date.
hypotheses.mechanism: Price impounds expectations continuously; only the deviation from expectation is new information. A macro LEVEL that is fully anticipated has zero information content on the day it prints, which is a coherent explanation for why 735 level/change tests produced exactly the chance rate of nominal hits — those features were mechanically incapable of carrying news. The surprise is a different object. The reason it might predict rather than be instantly arbitraged: claims surprises are a noisy signal whose informational content is only confirmed by subsequent weeks, so rational learners update gradually (Bayesian underreaction to noisy signals), producing multi-day drift in the surprise direction. Direction: a downside claims surprise (fewer claims than expected) is a positive growth shock — long equity indices, negative for gold via the real-rate channel.
hypotheses.data_needed: ALFRED/FRED vintage history for ICSA (weekly, 652 dev observations), plus PAYEMS, CPIAUCSL, INDPRO, UNRATE, PCEPILFE, UMCSENT (monthly, ~150 dev each). Retrieved via the free FRED API with realtime_start/realtime_end and output_type=2 to get the full vintage matrix. FRED release/dates endpoint for exact release timestamps. Price data already on disk. Optional cross-check: Cleveland Fed inflation nowcast for the CPI expectation.
hypotheses.how_to_test: 1) Pull the full vintage matrix per series. For each release date t, the information set is every vintage with realtime_start <= t-1. 2) Build the expectation with a rolling model refit only on pre-release vintages: for ICSA, a seasonal model on log-level with 52-week seasonality plus AR terms, estimated on the last 5 years of the then-current vintage; predict the reference week. 3) surprise = first_print - prediction, z-scored by the trailing 3-year rolling SD of that series' own past surprises (past only). 4) Trade at the CLOSE of the day AFTER realtime_start — FRED ingest can lag the wire by a business day, and this rule is conservative in the same spirit as PUB_LAG. 5) Weekly claims signal with a 5-trading-day horizon is NON-OVERLAPPING, so the t-stat needs no sqrt(h) deflation — this is the cleanest test in the set. Monthly series with a 20-day horizon are also non-overlapping. Deflate only where a horizon exceeds the release interval. 6) Apply the repo's standard per-turn cost model. 7) Dev window only, < 2022-07-01. 8) Count every series x asset x horizon cell in the BH-FDR pool alongside the existing 735 + 122 + all prior tests, and report the primary pre-registered cell separately from the exploratory grid.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: The 735 tests used qlab.macro.available(), which returns the as-of value forward-filled and lagged — a level or a diff of a level. None of those features contains an expectation term, so none of them is a surprise. ICSA appears in the dead list as a level/change; the weekly claims SURPRISE has never been constructed here, and requires vintage data that is not currently on disk at all. This is a different feature, not a re-parameterization of an old one.

hypotheses.name: Surprise-orthogonal release-day move reverses
hypotheses.claim: Decompose the release-day return into the component explained by the standardized surprise and the residual. The RESIDUAL — the part of the release-day move that the data does not justify — reverses over the following 1 to 3 days, while the surprise-explained component does not. Primary test: XAUUSD, CPI and NFP release days, residual from a rolling pre-fit regression of release-day return on surprise z, traded as a fade at the next close with a 3-day hold.
hypotheses.mechanism: A release day concentrates two very different things into one bar: genuine information, and forced flow (stop runs, gamma hedging, option expiry positioning, risk-limit-driven unwinds by anyone caught offside). Information is permanent; flow is transitory and reverses when the liquidity provider who absorbed it unwinds. The surprise z-score is an INSTRUMENT that identifies the informational component — it is measurable, exogenous to the market's own positioning, and known at the same instant. Whatever the price did beyond what the data justified is, by construction, the flow component, and flow-driven price pressure mean-reverts. This is the standard permanent/transitory decomposition, but instrumented with macro news rather than with order flow, which is the only version available to someone without tick data. Note this hypothesis explicitly does not require the market to underreact to news — it only requires that non-informational price pressure on high-volume days reverts, which is one of the more durable facts in market microstructure.
hypotheses.data_needed: The surprise z-scores from Hypothesis 1 (ALFRED vintages, free). Daily OHLC already on disk. FRED release/dates for release-day identification. Nothing further.
hypotheses.how_to_test: 1) For each release event, compute release-day return r_t (close-to-close on the release date). 2) Fit beta of r_t on surprise z using a strictly expanding/rolling window of PRIOR events only — never the full sample — to avoid in-sample beta contaminating the residual. 3) residual e_t = r_t - beta_{t-1} * z_t. 4) Signal = -sign(e_t) scaled by |e_t| / trailing residual SD, entered at the close of day t+1, held 1 and 3 days. 5) Native frequency is the release frequency; for CPI+NFP pooled that is ~300 dev events, for the full tier-1 set ~900 including weekly claims. Non-overlapping at 3 days for monthly releases; deflate by sqrt(3) if pooled events fall within 3 days of each other. 6) Critical falsification test that separates this from generic mean reversion: run the identical fade on the RAW release-day return with no surprise decomposition, and on a matched set of NON-release days with equal absolute return. If the raw fade and the non-release fade work equally well, the surprise instrument is adding nothing and the hypothesis is dead — it has been re-derived as ordinary short-horizon reversal. This falsification must be reported. 7) Costs applied; dev only; enters the same FDR pool.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: Nothing in the dead list decomposes a return using an exogenous news instrument. Candlestick and geometry work (122 tests) used only price shape; ML/AI work used price and candle geometry; the macro work used levels. This uses a macro surprise not as a directional predictor but as an identifying instrument to split one day's return into two economically distinct pieces, and trades only one of them. Also distinct from 'NFP-day holds' in the dead list, which was a directional calendar hold with no surprise and no decomposition.

hypotheses.name: News-density conditioning of the surviving MNQ daily momentum
hypotheses.claim: The MNQ daily-momentum survivor's edge is concentrated in stretches with LOW scheduled tier-1 macro-release density and degrades or inverts across high-density stretches. Gating the existing signal to flat on the N trading days spanning a dense release cluster raises the strategy's Sharpe and, more importantly, cuts its worst drawdown, without the gate itself being fitted to returns.
hypotheses.mechanism: Momentum profits arise from gradual information diffusion — the 'frog in the pan' result: information that arrives continuously and in small pieces produces sustained underreaction and durable trends, while information that arrives as a single discrete jump is priced immediately and produces no drift. Scheduled macro releases are precisely the discrete-jump case. Worse, they are the mechanism by which momentum CRASHES: a dense cluster of tier-1 data resolves macro uncertainty abruptly, which is when crowded trend positioning unwinds all at once. So the prediction is directional and asymmetric — momentum should earn less and lose more violently across release clusters. This is a conditioning hypothesis on a known survivor, not a new standalone edge.
hypotheses.data_needed: FRED release/dates endpoint (free, no vintages needed) for the scheduled dates of CPI, PPI, PAYEMS, GDP, PCE, retail sales, ISM proxies, plus fomc_dates.csv already on disk. The signal is the count of tier-1 releases in a forward window, which is published months in advance, so there is structurally zero lookahead. MNQ price and the existing strategy's daily return series, both already in the repo.
hypotheses.how_to_test: 1) Build density_t = weighted count of tier-1 scheduled releases in the window [t, t+2], weights fixed ex ante by release importance and NOT fitted (e.g. FOMC=3, CPI/NFP=2, everything else=1). Freeze these weights before looking at any return. 2) Primary test is a single regression on the survivor's existing daily returns: r_strategy_t = a + b * density_t + e, t-stat on b at daily frequency over the dev window only. This is one coefficient, one asset, one pre-registered specification — the cheapest possible FDR footprint in this whole set. 3) Only if b is significantly negative, evaluate the gated strategy: flat when density exceeds a threshold chosen as a fixed quantile (e.g. top tercile), not by search. Report Sharpe, max DD, and turnover change with costs. 4) The strategy's daily returns are serially overlapping if positions are multi-day, so cluster standard errors by holding period or deflate by sqrt(average holding days). 5) Never touch the holdout with this — the survivor's holdout Sharpe of 0.82 is already spent; the gate must be validated on dev and then submitted to holdout exactly once, if at all.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: Nothing in the dead list conditions any strategy on scheduled news density. Pre-FOMC drift, NFP-day holds and turn-of-month were all standalone directional calendar bets that had to generate their own alpha; this is an orthogonal conditioner on an already-validated signal, and it can succeed even if every calendar-day directional bet fails — indeed the fact that calendar directional bets all failed is consistent with this, since it predicts release days are informationally efficient, which is exactly why momentum should not work across them. It is also distinct from volume gating (dead), which used realized volume; this uses an ex-ante published schedule that cannot be contaminated by price.

hypotheses.name: Nowcast-revision as pre-aggregated growth news (GDPNow / ADS vintage delta)
hypotheses.claim: The day-over-day revision in the Atlanta Fed GDPNow estimate, and the vintage-to-vintage revision in the Philadelphia Fed ADS index, predict 1-to-5-day returns in ES/MNQ (positive) and XAUUSD (negative), with more power than any single release surprise because the revision aggregates the news content of everything that released that day into one growth-denominated number.
hypotheses.mechanism: A nowcast only moves when data arrives, and the size of its move is exactly how much a professional real-time model updated its view of the economy. That makes the revision a model-free, publicly-timestamped, correctly-weighted aggregation of the day's macro surprise — it solves the aggregation problem in Hypothesis 1 without me having to choose weights, which is where a DIY composite usually goes wrong. Economically, growth news should move cyclical assets up and the safe-haven/real-rate asset down. The reason drift might exist: nowcast revisions are published with a lag of hours to a day after the underlying release, so a slow-moving allocator reading the nowcast rather than the raw tape trades after the fact, and that staggered demand pushes prices in the same direction for several days.
hypotheses.data_needed: Atlanta Fed GDPNow historical vintages spreadsheet (free download, no API key, coverage from 2011). Philadelphia Fed ADS Business Conditions Index vintage archive (free download, no key). ADS is the higher-n input: it is dated daily with vintages roughly every business day, versus GDPNow's ~25 updates per year, so ADS is the primary and GDPNow the robustness check. Price data on disk.
hypotheses.how_to_test: 1) Load ADS vintages; for each publication date v, delta_v = ADS_v(latest common reference date) - ADS_{v-1}(same reference date), so the revision is measured on a FIXED reference point and is not contaminated by the index simply extending. 2) z-score delta by trailing 3-year SD of past revisions. 3) Trade at the close of the day after the vintage's publication date — publication timestamps must come from the file's own vintage labels, not from the reference date, and if a vintage's publication timestamp is ambiguous, add a full extra day. This is the single largest lookahead risk in the proposal and must be handled explicitly. 4) Horizons 1 and 5 days; ADS revisions are near-daily so a 5-day horizon overlaps 5x and the t-stat must be deflated by sqrt(5). 5) GDPNow revision as an independent confirmation on ~275 dev events, non-overlapping at 5 days. 6) Costs; dev only; joint FDR pool. 7) Honest dependency: if Hypothesis 1 fails badly across the board, this adds little independent information, since both are functions of the same underlying release surprises. Its value is diagnostic — it separates 'the aggregation was wrong' from 'there is no signal in macro surprises at all'.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: ADS and GDPNow are not in the 31 FRED series on disk and are not in the 38 features of the 735-test sweep. More importantly the object is categorically different: it is the first difference of a professional forecast, not the level or change of an observed macro quantity. The dead list contains no forecast-revision feature of any kind.

hypotheses.name: Back-revision direction as a limited-attention signal
hypotheses.claim: The revision to PRIOR months' data published inside a release — e.g. the two-month payroll revision printed alongside each NFP headline — predicts returns in the direction of the revision over the following 5 to 20 days, controlling for the headline surprise itself.
hypotheses.mechanism: Two facts have to both hold, and both are independently documented. First, statistical agency revisions are positively autocorrelated: BLS payroll revisions cluster in sign, especially around business-cycle turning points where the birth-death model systematically misses, so a negative revision this month raises the probability of a negative revision next month. That makes the revision genuinely predictive of the true state of the economy. Second, attention on release day is overwhelmingly allocated to the headline; the revision is a secondary number in the same press release, reported in the fifth paragraph, and gets far less algorithmic and human weight in the first minutes. Limited attention to a value that is both published and predictive is the classic setup for delayed price adjustment. The signal is the revision sign, and the horizon is longer than the surprise trade because the mechanism is slow re-rating, not immediate repricing.
hypotheses.data_needed: ALFRED vintages for PAYEMS (150 dev events), plus INDPRO and PCEPILFE as secondaries. The revision is computed directly from the vintage matrix: the value for reference month p as printed at release t, minus the value for the same month p as printed at release t-1. Free FRED API key. No other data.
hypotheses.how_to_test: 1) From the vintage matrix, revision_t = sum over the two prior reference months of (vintage_t value - vintage_{t-1} value), expressed in thousands of jobs, then z-scored by trailing 3-year SD of past revisions. 2) Primary test is a BIVARIATE regression of forward return on both the headline surprise z (from Hypothesis 1) and revision z, so the revision coefficient is estimated controlling for the headline — the whole claim is that the revision carries information the headline does not, and a univariate test cannot establish that. 3) Assets: MNQ and ES primary (labor-market re-rating is an equity-duration story), XAUUSD secondary. Horizons 5 and 20 days; NFP is monthly so a 20-day horizon is essentially non-overlapping, and 5-day is cleanly non-overlapping. 4) n = 150 is the binding constraint and I want this stated up front: a t=3 at 150 monthly observations requires ~0.85 annualized Sharpe from a once-a-month signal, and the estimator variance at that sample size is poor enough that a nominal pass here should be treated as weak evidence even before FDR. 5) Costs; dev only; joint FDR pool. 6) A useful precondition worth checking first, at zero cost: verify in the vintage data that payroll revisions actually ARE positively autocorrelated in 2010-2022. If that first-stage relationship is absent in the sample, the mechanism's first leg is broken and the return test should not be run at all — that saves an FDR slot.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: Revisions are not merely absent from the 735 tests, they are structurally invisible to the current data layer: qlab/macro.py loads a single non-vintage CSV per series, so the repo has literally never seen a first print, only final revised values. That also means every prior macro test carried a subtle revision-lookahead (using final values on dates when only the first print existed), which PUB_LAG does not fix. Building the vintage layer is worth doing for that reason alone, independent of whether this hypothesis works.

hypotheses.name: Fed intermeeting speech flow and tone
hypotheses.claim: The intensity and hawkish/dovish tilt of FOMC-voter speeches during the intermeeting window predicts 5-to-10-day returns in XAUUSD and MNQ: a cluster of hawkish speeches following a dovish market repricing predicts negative returns in both, and vice versa. The signal is the interaction of speech tone with the direction the market has already moved, not tone alone.
hypotheses.mechanism: Between meetings, speeches are the Fed's only steering instrument for expectations, and officials use them deliberately to push back when market pricing drifts away from the committee's intent. The interaction term is the whole point: hawkish speeches when the market is already hawkishly priced are confirmatory and carry no news, while hawkish speeches after a dovish repricing are corrective and carry a lot. That interaction structure is why tone alone has generally failed in the literature and why a level-of-tone feature would deserve to fail here too. The blackout period provides a clean natural placebo: from the second Saturday before an FOMC through the Thursday after, officials are barred from speaking, so the signal is mechanically zero and any apparent edge in that window is pure noise or a bug.
hypotheses.data_needed: BIS Central bankers' speeches dataset (free bulk download: date, speaker, institution, full text) and/or the Federal Reserve's own speech listing on federalreserve.gov, both free and scrapeable. FOMC voter roster by year (public, free, from FOMC meeting minutes). fomc_dates.csv on disk for blackout construction. Market-pricing-direction control from DGS2 already on disk.
hypotheses.how_to_test: 1) Filter the speech corpus to FOMC voting members in the speech year. 2) Score tone with a FIXED, pre-registered hawkish/dovish lexicon written before any return is examined and never tuned — this is the discipline that kills most text-signal work, and if the lexicon gets adjusted after seeing a backtest the result is worthless. 3) tone_t = weighted sum of scores over speeches in the trailing 10 calendar days, weighted by speaker seniority (Chair > Vice Chair > Governors > regional presidents), weights fixed ex ante. 4) market_drift_t = 10-day change in DGS2, lagged one day per PUB_LAG. 5) Signal = -tone_t * sign-mismatch with market_drift_t, i.e. active only when speech tone opposes recent rate repricing. 6) Native frequency is roughly weekly given speech clustering; horizons 5 and 10 days, deflate the 10-day t by sqrt(2) for overlap. 7) Placebo: run the identical construction restricted to blackout windows, where it must produce nothing. If it produces something, there is a date-alignment bug. 8) Costs; dev only; joint FDR pool. 9) Honest caveats: lexicon tone scoring is a crude proxy for what a speech actually communicates, speech text may need retrieval for the full dev window and coverage gaps are likely for regional presidents, and this is the proposal I would drop first if effort is constrained.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: The dead list includes pre-FOMC drift and FOMC-date effects, both of which are pure calendar bets on the meeting itself. This uses the intermeeting communication flow, which is a different information channel and is specifically the channel that operates when no meeting is scheduled. It is also not the previously-dead ML/AI work, which was applied to price and candle geometry, never to text. That said, I rate this lowest of the six: the mechanism is real but the measurement is weak, and a lexicon score is a lossy compression of the thing that actually matters.

result.lens: Flows and plumbing — forced, calendar-known money movement

hypotheses.name: Primary dealer Treasury inventory as intermediation capacity
hypotheses.claim: When primary dealers' net Treasury coupon position (NY Fed FR2004, PDPOSGSC-* summed, or PDPOSGST-TOT) sits in the top quintile of its trailing 104-week range, risk assets underperform over the following 1-4 weeks: sign-predicted negative mean return for MNQ/ES and elevated realized vol. Bottom quintile predicts the opposite. Native weekly signal, weekly-horizon claim.
hypotheses.mechanism: Dealers are obligated to bid at every Treasury auction, so inventory builds are substantially involuntary — the position is exogenous to their view, which is exactly what makes it a capacity variable rather than a sentiment variable. A stuffed balance sheet consumes VaR and SLR capacity, and that capacity is shared across every market the same desks intermediate. Intermediary asset pricing (He-Kelly-Manela, Adrian-Etula-Muir) says the marginal investor's constraint, not the representative agent's, sets risk premia. Distinct from a positioning/sentiment signal: the prediction is about the price of risk-bearing services, not about who is right.
hypotheses.data_needed: NY Fed markets API primary dealer statistics (FR2004): https://markets.newyorkfed.org/api/pd/get/<SERIES>.csv — verified HTTP 200, no key. PDPOSGS-B (bills) and PDPOSGSC-* (coupons by maturity bucket) available from 2013-04-03 onward (post-FR2004-revision vintage; earlier vintage exists under different codes with a definitional break at 2013). Series catalogue at /api/pd/list/timeseries.json returns 1,539 codes. Prices already on disk (data/daily/*.csv).
hypotheses.how_to_test: Pull weekly as-of-Wednesday levels. PUB_LAG: FR2004 is released the Thursday of the FOLLOWING week — add a conservative 10 calendar days to the as-of date in qlab/macro.py PUB_LAG before any use, so a Wed as-of value is first tradable the subsequent Monday. Normalize to a trailing 104w percentile (a level is non-stationary; the percentile is the capacity claim). Regress next-1w and next-4w returns on the percentile at NATIVE WEEKLY frequency (no daily upsampling — that manufactures fake N). Report Newey-West t with lag = horizon, and deflate the 4w overlapping t by sqrt(4). Dev only (<2022-07-01), giving ~480 weekly observations. Costs: one round trip per weekly rebalance at the FROZEN_SPEC per-side rates. Append every config to research/ledger.jsonl and BH-correct within the new family; the honest comparison is against the existing 735-test family.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: Zero grep hits for 'primary dealer' anywhere in the repo. The 735 macro tests were all demand-side, liquidity-quantity, growth, inflation or price-of-risk series — none measured intermediary balance-sheet state. COT (data/external/cot_weekly.csv, run_cot.py, the COT_NQ_washout leg) is a different agent (speculators), a different market (futures), and a different mechanism (crowding/sentiment mean-reversion) from dealer capacity in cash Treasuries.

hypotheses.name: Treasury coupon auction concession cycle
hypotheses.claim: Between a coupon auction's announcement and its settlement, long-duration assets cheapen and then richen on a fixed, publicly known schedule. Specifically: TLT (and IEF) earn negative excess returns from announcement date to auction date, and positive excess returns from the auction-day close to +3 sessions; the effect scales with that auction's offering amount relative to its own trailing 8-auction average and is concentrated in the 10y/30y tenors. Daily horizon, ~120 tradable events per year.
hypotheses.mechanism: This is the cleanest forced flow in the entire fixed income calendar. Dealers must absorb a pre-announced quantity of duration on a pre-announced date, and their risk-bearing capacity is finite and price-inelastic over a three-day window. They pre-hedge by selling duration into the auction (pushing yields up, the 'concession'), then unwind as the paper distributes. The flow is mandatory and the schedule is public, so the price pressure is a liquidity premium paid to dealers, not information. Lou, Yan & Zhang (RFS 2013) document exactly this in Treasuries — and also warn it has decayed, which is a real reason for a low prior rather than a high one.
hypotheses.data_needed: TreasuryDirect auction API: https://www.treasurydirect.gov/TA_WS/securities/search?format=json&startDate=...&endDate=...&dateFieldName=auctionDate — verified working, returned 21 records for Jan-2015 alone with announcementDate, auctionDate, issueDate, securityType, securityTerm and offeringAmount. No key, full history. Instruments: data/external/etf_TLT_1d.csv and etf_IEF_1d.csv (from 2009) already on disk; DGS10/DGS30 on disk for a yield-space version.
hypotheses.how_to_test: Build the auction calendar, keep securityType=='Note'/'Bond' (drop bills — no duration). No lookahead: the size is learned at the ANNOUNCEMENT (usually 11:00 ET), so use announcementDate + 1 session as first tradable date. Test in yield space FIRST (DGS10/DGS30 changes over each window) — that isolates the mechanism from ETF frictions, and if it fails there the tradable version cannot work. Then test on TLT/IEF net of costs. Because auctions in a month overlap, define non-overlapping event windows or use a stationary block bootstrap (L=20, B=2000, matching qlab/metrics.py) rather than a naive pooled t. Report the size-scaled version and the unscaled version as two separate ledger entries, and BH-correct. Report the equity/gold spillover (MNQ, ES, XAUUSD over the same windows) as a SEPARATE, lower-prior family — do not let it borrow significance from the bond result. Dev only.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: The only 'auction' hits in the repo are market-microstructure auction theory in run_volume.py (rejected volume/auction gating) — nothing to do with Treasury auctions. Not a calendar-day effect: auction dates are keyed to tenor rotation and refunding weeks, so it is not day-of-month and is not the falsified turn-of-month. Nothing supply-side appeared in the 735 macro tests.

hypotheses.name: Duration supply shock from the coupon/bill issuance mix
hypotheses.claim: The rolling 4-week quantity of 10y-equivalent duration Treasury announces to the market predicts term premium and long-duration asset returns over the following 1-4 weeks. Rising 10y-equivalent supply predicts negative returns for TLT and for MNQ RELATIVE to ES (long-duration equity underperforms short-duration equity); falling supply predicts the reverse. Signal changes meaningfully only at quarterly refunding, so the honest native frequency is quarterly-to-monthly, not daily.
hypotheses.mechanism: Preferred-habitat / limited arbitrage: the marginal buyer of 30y duration is not the marginal buyer of a 4-week bill, so shifting the issuance mix toward coupons forces a specific, price-inelastic clientele to absorb duration and raises the term premium. This is the one lever in the whole complex that is set by an entity with no profit motive and announced in advance — Treasury's coupon-vs-bill decision at the Quarterly Refunding Announcement. The equity leg follows mechanically: a higher discount rate hits long-duration cash flows (Nasdaq) harder than short-duration ones (S&P value tilt), giving a spread trade that is neutral to the general equity drift.
hypotheses.data_needed: Same TreasuryDirect auction endpoint (verified free). Construct 10y-equivalent supply = sum over announced auctions in the trailing 20 sessions of offeringAmount x (approximate modified duration of that tenor / duration of the 10y). Duration approximations from the tenor alone are adequate; no yield curve fitting needed. Markets: MNQ, ES, XAUUSD on disk; TLT/IEF on disk.
hypotheses.how_to_test: Timestamp every auction at its announcementDate (that is when the size becomes public), lag one session. Because the variable is highly persistent, the effective sample is the number of independent issuance-mix CHANGES (~50 quarterly revisions in the dev window), NOT 3,000 daily observations — state that effective N explicitly and compute t at the quarterly/monthly change frequency, then deflate any overlapping-return t by sqrt(h). Test three legs separately with the sign declared in advance: (a) TLT/DGS10 term premium response, (b) MNQ-minus-ES vol-scaled spread, (c) XAUUSD. Each is one ledger entry; BH across all of them plus the 735 already run. Dev only, costs applied per FROZEN_SPEC.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: The 735 tests contained no supply-side variable at all — every one was a demand, liquidity, growth, inflation or risk-price series. GFDEBTN (federal debt) was tested but is a quarterly STOCK with a 90-day publication lag, which cannot see the coupon/bill MIX or its announcement timing. THREEFYTP10 (term premium) was tested as an outcome/feature, never as something driven by a measurable forced supply. Zero grep hits for refunding, QRA or buyback.

hypotheses.name: Monthly options-expiration gamma cycle as a mean-reversion gate
hypotheses.claim: Realized index volatility is systematically lower in the four sessions ending on monthly OPEX (third Friday) than in the four sessions immediately after, and one-day return reversal in ES/MNQ is profitable in the pre-OPEX window and absent or negative in the post-OPEX window. The tradable form is a gate: run mean-reversion sizing pre-OPEX, trend/flat sizing post-OPEX. Daily signal, ~150 cycles in the dev window.
hypotheses.mechanism: Index option open interest piles up at monthly expiries, and the structural supply of index optionality (overwriting, put-selling, structured-product issuance) leaves dealers net long gamma in SPX. Long-gamma delta hedging is mechanically contrarian — dealers sell into rallies and buy dips to stay flat — which compresses realized vol and manufactures short-horizon mean reversion. On expiry that gamma disappears from the book at once and the damper is removed. The hedging is forced by risk limits, not by any view, and the removal date is fixed by the exchange calendar.
hypotheses.data_needed: Nothing to fetch: the third-Friday calendar is derivable from the existing daily index. Prices already on disk (ES.csv, MNQ.csv). NOTE THE HONEST LIMIT: true dealer gamma exposure requires historical option open interest, which is NOT free (CBOE/OptionMetrics charge for it). Only the calendar proxy is testable here, and the calendar proxy is a strictly weaker instrument for the mechanism — which is the main reason the prior is low rather than moderate.
hypotheses.how_to_test: Two claims, tested and corrected separately. (1) Vol claim: variance ratio of realized vol in sessions [-4,0] vs [+1,+4] around each monthly OPEX, paired by cycle, tested with a paired block bootstrap across ~150 dev cycles. This has real power and is the honest first gate — if the vol asymmetry is absent, the return claim has no mechanism left. (2) Return/gating claim: a one-day reversal signal on ES and MNQ, its Sharpe estimated separately in the two windows, difference tested by block bootstrap; costs charged per FROZEN_SPEC (MNQ 0.25+0.50+0.31 points per side is brutal for a daily reversal system and will very likely kill it even if the statistic is real). Confounder to remove explicitly: quarterly triple-witching months differ from serial months, and OPEX week overlaps the mid-month coupon settlement — run the test excluding March/June/September/December to check the effect is not one subsample. Dev only; BH-correct with the calendar-effect family (turn-of-month, session drifts) since these test related structure.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: Zero grep hits for opex, expiry or expiration anywhere in the repo, and it is not in the FROZEN_SPEC falsified list. Distinct from the falsified turn-of-month (calendar month boundary, retail/pension inflow story) and from session drifts (time-of-day). Distinct from the failed VIX and vol-term-structure gates: those gate on the LEVEL of implied vol, this gates on a fixed calendar position that proxies a dealer hedging obligation.

hypotheses.name: The PRICE of reserves, not the quantity
hypotheses.claim: The spread of the overnight rate over the Fed's administered floor — EFFR minus IOER (2010-2021), spliced to SOFR minus IORB (2021+) — predicts risk-asset returns over the next 5-20 sessions with a negative sign: when overnight money trades ABOVE the floor, reserves are genuinely scarce, dealer funding is dear, and MNQ/ES/XAUUSD underperform. The 20-session z-score of the spread is the signal.
hypotheses.mechanism: September 2019 is the whole argument. Reserve balances were at levels the Fed itself called 'ample' by every quantity metric — and repo printed 10%. Quantity of reserves is a bad proxy for scarcity because it ignores distribution across banks and the regulatory constraints that make reserves non-fungible. The price at which the marginal bank borrows overnight is the market's own direct measurement of that scarcity, and it moves BEFORE the quantity aggregates do. When funding is dear, dealers shrink inventory and haircuts widen, which raises the required return on every financed position — gold especially, since carrying it is a financing trade.
hypotheses.data_needed: FRED, all verified HTTP 200 and free: EFFR (from 2000-07), IOER (2008-10-09 to 2021-07-28), IORB (2021-07-29 onward), SOFR (2018-04-03 onward). Splice IOER->IORB at the 2021-07-28 handover for a continuous floor covering the entire dev window. Prices on disk.
hypotheses.how_to_test: PUB_LAG = 1 day (NY Fed publishes the prior day's EFFR/SOFR around 08:00 ET; administered floor rates are known in advance). Daily signal, 5d and 20d horizons, Newey-West t deflated by sqrt(h). CRITICAL HONESTY CHECK, do this before anything else: plot the spread and count the days it is materially away from zero. From 2010-2018 EFFR was pinned in a QE-flooded corridor with almost no variation, so the informative sample is concentrated in roughly 2018-2019 and 2021-2022 — perhaps 400 useful days inside a 3,100-day dev window. Report that effective N with the result, and if the entire t-stat is generated by the September 2019 repo episode plus March 2020, declare it dead rather than dressing it as a regime. Also test the corridor-position version (EFFR percentile between the RRP award rate and IORB), which has variation across more of the sample. Dev only, costs applied, BH-corrected against the 735.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: Zero grep hits for SOFR, IOER, IORB, EFFR or repo in the repo. Every liquidity variable in the 735 tests was a QUANTITY — WALCL, WRESBAL, WTREGEN, RRPONTSYD, and the net-liquidity combination. DFF (fed funds) was tested but as a POLICY RATE CHANGE, i.e. a stance variable, never differenced against the floor to make a scarcity spread. The whole point is that the quantity family failing is weak evidence about the price family, because quantity and price of reserves decoupled repeatedly in this exact sample.

hypotheses.name: Decomposed TGA drain: tax inflows are contractionary, issuance inflows are not
hypotheses.claim: Only the tax-driven component of TGA inflows drains bank reserves. Using the Daily Treasury Statement to isolate 'Individual Income and Employment Taxes, Not Withheld' plus 'Corporation Income Taxes' deposits, a large tax inflow (>2 sigma of its trailing 1y daily distribution, which occurs in tight clusters around Jan 15 / Apr 15 / Jun 15 / Sep 15) predicts negative MNQ/ES returns over the following 5-10 sessions and a partial recovery over the following 15-25 sessions as Treasury spends the balance back down.
hypotheses.mechanism: A tax payment is a genuine, forced transfer of a deposit from a private bank account to the Fed's account: private-sector bank reserves fall one-for-one and there is no offsetting asset created for the private sector. An identically sized TGA inflow funded by a bill auction that money market funds pay for out of the reverse repo facility is reserve-NEUTRAL — cash simply moves from one Fed liability to another. This is precisely why the linear net-liquidity test failed: WALCL - TGA - RRP treats those two flows as the same thing when they are opposite in economic effect. Tax dates are also fixed in statute, so the flow is forced, dated years in advance, and cannot be timed away by the payer.
hypotheses.data_needed: Treasury Fiscal Data DTS API, verified working with no key: /v1/accounting/dts/deposits_withdrawals_operating_cash (returned 63 categorized rows for 2019-04-15, including the individual and corporate tax deposit lines and the IRS refund withdrawal lines) and /v1/accounting/dts/operating_cash_balance for the daily TGA level. History back to ~2005. RRPONTSYD and WRESBAL already on disk for the neutrality control.
hypotheses.how_to_test: PUB_LAG = 2 calendar days (DTS posts around 16:00 ET the next business day; 2 days is conservative). Build the daily tax-deposit series, standardize against its own trailing 1y distribution. STATE THE REAL SAMPLE SIZE: although the series is daily, its variation is concentrated in roughly 4-6 clusters per year, so the effective independent event count is ~50-60 in the dev window, not 3,100 — compute event-study statistics at that event frequency with a block bootstrap, never a pooled daily t. Declare the sign in advance (negative at 5-10d, positive at 15-25d) and treat a sign flip as failure, not as a finding. Two controls that must be run or the result means nothing: (a) rerun with issuance-funded TGA inflows as the regressor — the hypothesis REQUIRES that leg to be null, so a significant result there falsifies the mechanism rather than supporting it; (b) drop 2020 and 2018 and check the effect is not two tax seasons that happened to sit next to unrelated drawdowns. Dev only, costs applied, BH across the whole liquidity family including the 735.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: TGA was tested in the 735, but only as the WEEKLY WTREGEN level and change with a 3-day lag — a weekly series smears a two-day tax spike into noise, and the level cannot distinguish a tax drain from an issuance inflow. The DTS decomposition is a different dataset at a different frequency measuring a different object. Not the falsified turn-of-month: tax dates are the 15th of four specific months. The core claim is a direct, falsifiable diagnosis of WHY the net-liquidity test returned zero, which makes it worth one clean test even at a low prior.

result.lens:
NON-LINEARITY AND REGIME INTERACTION, with a hard power filter applied first.

Every macro test in this repo so far has been a *global monotone* test: Spearman IC over the full sample, top-vs-bottom tertile, or sign(z-score) held. All three are exactly zero under the most economically plausible macro data-generating process — one where the variable's effect on price is state-dependent and flips or vanishes outside a regime. A variable that predicts +40bp in 8% of days and 0bp in the other 92% has an IC of ~0.02 and a tertile spread of ~3bp. The 735-test sweep could not have found such a thing even if it were there. That is the gap I am aiming at.

Before proposing anything, I applied a discipline that killed more ideas than it kept: **a conditional hypothesis is only testable if the CONDITIONING VARIABLE CYCLES MANY TIMES INSIDE THE 12-YEAR DEV WINDOW.** The independent unit of evidence is the episode, not the day. I explicitly rejected these otherwise-attractive ideas on power grounds:
- Sahm-rule / recession-threshold crossing: exactly ONE crossing in dev (2020). Zero power.
- Stock-bond correlation regime as a signal-flipper: the correlation was negative for essentially all of dev and only turned in 2021-22. The interaction is unidentifiable before the holdout.
- RRP-buffer gating of net liquidity ("QT only bites when the RRP is drained"): the gate is ON for ~90% of dev (RRP was ~0 until Mar 2021), so the interaction is collinear with the main effect on dev and only separates in holdout. Untestable where it must be tested.
- Net-liquidity *acceleration* with a dead-zone: the natural window is quarterly, giving ~48 non-overlapping observations. Dreadful power.
- 5y5y inflation un-anchoring: 2 episodes, both confounded.

I also measured, rather than assumed, the episode count for the one credit-based hypothesis I did keep: at a 10-day divergence window and z>1.0 there are ~35 independent episodes on dev (at z>1.5, only ~10 — which is why I pre-declare the looser threshold). A related honest constraint that shapes several proposals: credit/vol/liquidity conditioners produce MARKET-WIDE episodes on the same calendar dates, so pooling the same conditioner across 7 markets adds almost no independent information. Only positioning data (COT, per-contract) and event-day data genuinely multiply the sample.

The six below are ordered by how much genuinely independent evidence they can produce. Each is specified as ONE pre-declared functional form with a stated multiplicity cost (1-3 tests), not a grid — a conditional hypothesis with free parameters is a snooping machine, and the whole point of adding non-linearity is that it makes overfitting easier, not harder.

hypotheses.name: COT_CROWD_DISPERSION (positioning extremes reverse only when held by MANY SMALL traders)
hypotheses.claim: The COT washout/fade effect is not a function of position size at all — it is a function of WHO holds the position. Define, for each contract-week: p = z-score (104w) of net-noncommercial position / open interest; and on the crowded side, s = contracts per noncommercial trader (NC_short / Traders-NC-Short when p<0, NC_long / Traders-NC-Long when p>0), z-scored over 104w. CLAIM: forward 1-week return in the fade direction is positive when |p| > 1.5 AND s_z < 0 (a diffuse crowd of many small holders), and is zero or negative when |p| > 1.5 AND s_z > 0 (a concentrated position held by few large holders). The interaction term −sign(p)·|p|·(−s_z) carries a positive pooled coefficient while the main effect −sign(p)·|p| does not.
hypotheses.mechanism: Net position size conflates two opposite things. A large net short built by 40 traders averaging 3,000 lots each is a levered conviction position taken by informed, well-capitalised institutions — it persists, and fading it is fading informed capital. The same net short built by 160 traders averaging 700 lots each is a consensus trade held by weak hands with tight risk limits — it is the crowd, and it unwinds violently on the first adverse move because each holder is individually small, marginally capitalised, and stops out. Trader COUNT and average size per trader separate these; net position alone cannot. This is the standard 'crowded trade fragility' mechanism (Stein 2009 on crowding, Barroso-Santa-Clara on momentum crashes) and it makes a prediction the repo has already partly observed without explanation: the NQ/SPX spec-short washout worked (index shorts in 2010-2020 were overwhelmingly a diffuse retail/CTA crowd) while the same rule failed on EUR, GBP, USDJPY, gold and silver (where the noncommercial side is dominated by a handful of large macro funds). The interaction predicts the cross-market pattern that the main effect cannot.
hypotheses.data_needed: Already on disk: data/external/cot/deacot{1999..2026}.zip. The parsing machinery exists (run_cot_breadth.py). The needed columns have NEVER been read by any script in this repo: field 77 Traders-Total(All), 78 Traders-Noncommercial-Long(All), 79 Traders-Noncommercial-Short(All), and 101-108 the concentration ratios (Gross/Net share of largest 4 and 8 traders, long and short). Verified present and populated (e.g. GOLD 2015-12-29: OI 401,880, NC_L 150,229, NC_S 131,127, Traders-NC-L 118, Traders-NC-S 119, Conc-Gross-4-Long 21.6%, Conc-Gross-4-Short 28.9%). Prices for the 9 mapped markets already loaded by run_cot_breadth.py.
hypotheses.how_to_test: ONE pre-declared pooled test, 2 tests total added to the ledger. (1) Rebuild the weekly panel for the 9 markets already covered by run_cot_breadth.py, keeping the existing no-lookahead timing exactly as-is (report as-of Tuesday, public Friday, position from the following Monday — do not touch it). (2) Compute p and s_z as defined, both from 104-week trailing windows using only data available at the report date. (3) Pooled panel regression of the forward 1-week return on: the main effect −sign(p)·|p|·1[|p|>1.5], the interaction −sign(p)·|p|·1[|p|>1.5]·(−s_z), and market fixed effects; standard errors clustered by DATE (this is essential — positioning extremes cluster on the same weeks across markets, so date-clustering is what prevents the pooled t from being inflated by cross-sectional dependence). (4) EXCLUDE NQ entirely from the primary test: the base washout leg was discovered there and is already in the book, so including it would recycle the discovery sample. NQ is used only as an out-of-sample sign check afterwards. (5) Report the count of independent episodes (weeks with |p|>1.5, deduplicated to blocks ≥4 weeks apart) per market before looking at any return. (6) Secondary, pre-declared, one test: the same interaction using Concentration-Net-4-Short/Long instead of contracts-per-trader, as an independent operationalisation of the same construct — if the two disagree, the finding is noise. Signal is weekly, t-stat at weekly frequency, no overlap deflation needed. Costs: the leg is a 1-week hold, use the existing COST_RT dict. Dev only (<2022-07-01). Pass criterion declared in advance: interaction t > 2.5 with date-clustered SE, correct sign in ≥6 of 8 non-NQ markets, and the main effect insignificant once the interaction is in.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: The COT work in this repo used exactly two constructs: z-score of net-spec/OI (contrarian) and its 4-week change (flow), applied to 3 then 9 markets. Trader counts, average position per trader, and concentration ratios have never been read out of the zip files — I confirmed by grep that no run script touches fields 77-124. This is not a re-run of the washout leg with a filter bolted on; it is a different measurement of crowding that makes a falsifiable prediction about the ALREADY-OBSERVED cross-market failure pattern (worked on NQ/SPX, failed on FX and metals). It is also not a macro-lag test at all, so it sits outside the 735-test family entirely.

hypotheses.name: MACRO_ORTHOGONAL_REVERSAL (only the part of the price move the macro driver does NOT explain reverts)
hypotheses.claim: The repo's central finding — macro drivers are contemporaneous, lagged correlation ~0.00 — is being read as 'macro is useless for prediction'. The correct reading is that the macro-EXPLAINED component of a price move is information (a random walk, no reversal) while the ORTHOGONAL residual is flow (price pressure, mean-reverting). CLAIM: for each market, decompose the daily return into r_t = β̂_t·Δd_t + e_t where d is the market's pre-declared contemporaneous driver and β̂ is a rolling 250-day OLS beta estimated only on data up to t−1. Then the 5-day cumulative RESIDUAL Σe predicts the next 5-day return with a NEGATIVE coefficient, the 5-day cumulative EXPLAINED component Σβ̂Δd predicts it with a coefficient indistinguishable from zero, and — the discriminating test — the residual's reversal coefficient is significantly LARGER IN MAGNITUDE than that of the raw 5-day return.
hypotheses.mechanism: A price move caused by a change in the discount rate or the dollar is a repricing of fundamentals: it should persist, because the new fundamental is the new fundamental. A price move of the same size that occurs while the fundamental driver did nothing — or moved the wrong way — was caused by someone needing to trade for a non-informational reason: a fund liquidating, an index rebalance, a margin call, a vol-target cutting notional, a dealer absorbing a one-sided flow. Liquidity providers demand compensation for absorbing that inventory and are paid back as the inventory is worked off, which takes days (Campbell-Grossman-Wang 1993; Nagel 2012 on the return to liquidity provision; Hendershott-Menkveld on price pressure). This is the textbook reason reversal exists, and it says the reversal signal should be the RESIDUAL, not the return. Every study that regresses forward return on the macro LEVEL is asking the wrong question: the level is public and priced; the residual is a flow imbalance that is not yet unwound.
hypotheses.data_needed: All on disk. Prices: data/daily/*.csv. Drivers, with the repo's existing PUB_LAG respected: XAUUSD → DFII10 (10y TIPS real yield) and DTWEXBGS (broad dollar); ES and MNQ → VIXCLS; EURUSD → DTWEXBGS; USDJPY → DGS10 (US 10y; NOT DEXJPUS, which is the price itself); WTIUSD → DTWEXBGS; JPXJPY → VIXCLS. Driver-market pairings are pre-declared from the repo's own Round-3 contemporaneous R² finding (gold/real-yields, indices/VIX, EURUSD/dollar), not selected on forward-return performance.
hypotheses.how_to_test: ONE pre-declared specification, 3 coefficients from a single regression per market, 7 markets = 7 tests. (1) All drivers enter with their existing PUB_LAG from qlab/macro.py (DFII10 and VIXCLS lag 1 day, DTWEXBGS lag 4), so the decomposition for day t−1 uses only information a trader had at the close of day t−1, and the position is taken at the day-t open. This costs one day of the signal and is non-negotiable. (2) β̂_t from a 250-day rolling OLS of r on Δd using data strictly before t; require ≥200 valid observations. (3) Build S_resid = −z(Σ_{5d} e), S_expl = −z(Σ_{5d} β̂Δd), S_raw = −z(r_5d), all z-scored on a trailing 252-day window. (4) Single multivariate regression of the forward 5-day return on S_resid and S_expl jointly (NOT separately — the point is which one carries the information when both are present), Newey-West SE with 5 lags, and the reported t deflated by sqrt(5) for the 5-day overlap per house rules. (5) The DISCRIMINATING test, declared before running, because without it this hypothesis collapses into plain daily mean-reversion which the repo has already killed on EURUSD and MNQ: stationary block-bootstrap (block length 20) the difference between the S_resid coefficient and the S_raw coefficient; the hypothesis is only interesting if that difference is positive with a bootstrap p < 0.05 in at least 4 of 7 markets. If S_resid ≈ S_raw, the macro decomposition is doing nothing and the answer is 'no, this is just reversal, which we already know is dead'. (6) Tradeable leg: vol-targeted 10%, 5-day hold, existing COST dict, dev only. Note the macro R² is only 16-40%, so the residual is most of the return by construction — step (5) is what makes this a real test rather than a relabelling.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: The 735-test sweep regressed forward returns on macro LEVELS and CHANGES. It never once used the macro variable to decompose the price series itself. The candlestick and ML studies used price geometry (OHLC shapes, ranges, returns) — never price orthogonalised to an exogenous economic variable. The gold/silver ratio test was a cross-sectional spread whose costs killed it; this is a single-instrument directional signal at half the cost. Most importantly, this hypothesis takes the repo's own strongest negative result (contemporaneous R² 16-43%, lagged 0.00) and uses it as an INPUT rather than treating it as a dead end — the contemporaneous beta is precisely what is needed to build the residual.

hypotheses.name: CREDIT_EQUITY_DIVERGENCE_HINGE (credit leads equity only when the two DISAGREE, and only on the downside)
hypotheses.claim: HY credit spreads carry no unconditional information about forward equity returns — because credit normally widens at the same time equity falls, and that joint move is already priced. The information is entirely in the DISAGREEMENT. Define, using traded ETF prices (no publication lag): C = 10-day log return of HYG/IEF (the credit-risk premium, duration-hedged), E = 10-day log return of ES; D = [z_252(E) − z_252(C)] / sqrt(2). CLAIM: forward 10-day ES/MNQ return is negative and economically large when D > 1.0 (credit deteriorating while equity holds up), while the SYMMETRIC condition D < −1.0 (credit healing while equity falls) carries NO positive predictive coefficient. The functional form is a one-sided hinge: signal = −max(D − 1.0, 0), with the coefficient on the mirrored hinge +max(−D − 1.0, 0) pre-declared to be insignificant.
hypotheses.mechanism: Equity and high-yield credit are claims on the same firm value, so a divergence between them is a genuine disagreement about the same cash flows, not two unrelated assets drifting apart. When they disagree, the credit market is the one to believe, for a structural reason: HY is where levered, informed, institutionally-constrained capital transacts first, and because it is less liquid, a move there requires actual risk transfer rather than sentiment. Equity — with retail flow, buybacks, index inflows and a far larger noise-trader base — can float above deteriorating fundamentals for weeks. The asymmetry is the load-bearing part of the claim: the mechanism is a default/leverage channel, which is convex and one-sided. Credit widening while equity is complacent means the option on firm value is being repriced downward and equity must catch down; the converse (credit healing while equity falls) is just equity noise, because there is no analogous forcing mechanism upward. A signal that works in both directions would be evidence AGAINST the mechanism and for data mining.
hypotheses.data_needed: All on disk, zero acquisition cost: data/external/etf_HYG_1d.csv, etf_IEF_1d.csv (both from 2009), data/daily/ES.csv, data/daily/MNQ.csv. Deliberately using traded ETF closes rather than BAMLH0A0HYM2 — the OAS index is a stale-priced, revised, matrix-priced index that carries a 2-day publication lag in PUB_LAG, whereas HYG/IEF are executable prices with no lag and no revision. IEF is the duration hedge that turns HYG into a pure credit-risk signal rather than a rates signal.
hypotheses.how_to_test: ONE pre-declared hinge specification, 2 markets, 2 tests. CRITICAL PRE-STEP, already done: I measured the episode count on dev before proposing this, because it is the binding constraint. At a 10-day window with z>1.0 there are 109 signal days forming ~35 independent episodes (blocks ≥10 days apart) on dev; at z>1.5 only ~10 episodes, which is unusable. The threshold is therefore FIXED AT 1.0 in advance and will not be tuned — tuning it is the obvious way this hypothesis becomes a lie. (1) Regress the forward 10-day ES return on three terms jointly: the positive hinge −max(D−1,0), the mirrored hinge +max(−D−1,0), and z_252(E) alone as a control (this control is mandatory: without it the hinge could be capturing nothing but short-term reversal after a rally, which is already known dead). (2) t-stats deflated by sqrt(10) for overlap; inference by stationary block-bootstrap with block length 20 days, and additionally an EPISODE-level t-test on ~35 non-overlapping episode returns, which is the honest number. (3) Report the power calculation up front: with 35 episodes and a 10-day ES vol near 2.5%, reaching t=2.5 requires roughly 105bp per episode. If the effect is smaller than that, this test cannot detect it and the correct conclusion is 'underpowered', not 'no effect'. (4) MNQ as the confirmatory sibling only. (5) Do NOT pool across the other 5 markets to inflate n — credit divergence episodes occur on the same calendar dates everywhere, so cross-market pooling adds dependent observations and a fraudulent-looking t. Dev only, existing COST dict, 10-day hold.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: The sweep tested hy_oas and ig_oas as levels and 4-week changes, via global Spearman and top-vs-bottom tertile — all of which average a rare, one-sided, market-wide event across 3,600 days and mechanically produce ~0. The HYG/IEF traded pair has never been constructed in this repo (the ETF files exist but are used only in the breadth/ERC portfolio work). Critically, this is a RELATIVE-STATE signal between two assets, not a macro level: the hinge is on the disagreement, and the mirrored-hinge null is a built-in falsification test that a fishing expedition would not survive.

hypotheses.name: ANNOUNCEMENT_DAY_STATE_INTERACTION (the macro premium is earned in ~24 days a year, with a state-dependent sign)
hypotheses.claim: Macro state variables appear to have zero predictive power over a 20-day horizon because the effect is not spread over 20 days — it is concentrated in the two or three SCHEDULED RELEASE DAYS inside that window, and diluted to invisibility by the other 17. CLAIM, in two parts. (a) BASE: pooled ES/MNQ returns on scheduled macro announcement days (FOMC decision days, NFP release days, CPI release days — roughly 24 per year) are materially higher than on non-announcement days. (b) THE REAL CLAIM, an interaction: the announcement-day premium is INCREASING in the tightness of financial conditions — specifically it loads positively on z(4-week change in NFCI) measured at the last release before the announcement — while the same state variable has no relation to returns on non-announcement days. Functional form: r_t = a + b·A_t + c·state_{t−1} + d·(A_t × state_{t−1}) + e, where A_t is the announcement-day indicator; the hypothesis lives entirely in d.
hypotheses.mechanism: Announcement-day risk premia are one of the more replicated results in asset pricing (Savor-Wilson 2013: a majority of the equity premium accrues on the ~15 scheduled macro announcement days per year; Lucca-Moench for the FOMC subset). The economics is that investors cannot avoid bearing the macro risk that resolves at a known instant, so they must be paid for holding through it — and the compensation is a premium collected on the day, not a forecast of the surprise. The interaction follows directly and is the part that is testable and not already in the literature in this form: the price of risk is not constant. When financial conditions are tightening — intermediaries constrained, risk appetite low — the compensation demanded for holding through a scheduled resolution of macro uncertainty is HIGHER, so the announcement-day premium should be larger exactly when the state variable says conditions are tight. This inverts the usual reading of NFCI: it does not tell you where the market is going, it tells you how much you get paid for bearing event risk. It also explains cleanly why nfci_chg4w showed up nominally in the failed sweep on some markets but never survived — the effect is real but concentrated in ~10% of days, so a full-sample regression divides it by ten.
hypotheses.data_needed: FOMC dates: already on disk, data/external/fomc_dates.csv (132 dates, 2010-2026). NFCI: already on disk with a conservative 6-day PUB_LAG. Prices: on disk. NFP and CPI HISTORICAL RELEASE DATES are the one item not on disk: obtainable free from ALFRED (FRED's vintage database, fred/series/vintagedates for PAYEMS and CPIAUCSL) which needs a free API key — a registration, not a payment. Fallback if the key is unwanted: NFP is the first Friday of the month with well-documented exceptions, and CPI is a published monthly schedule; but the heuristic misdates a handful of months and I would rather use the true vintage dates than hand-code exceptions. Flagging this honestly: everything else here is on disk, this one series needs a free registration.
hypotheses.how_to_test: One pooled regression, 2 pre-declared coefficients (b and d), on 2 markets = 4 tests. (1) Build the announcement calendar; verify the count is near 24/year and that no date is derived from anything except a published schedule (a release date that was itself inferred from the data would be a subtle lookahead). (2) Signal frequency is DAILY and the holding period is ONE DAY, so no overlap deflation is needed and the t-stat is honest at its native frequency — this is a large advantage over every 20-day macro test in the sweep, where sqrt(20) deflation destroyed everything. (3) Regress the daily ES return on A_t, state_{t−1}, and their interaction, with heteroskedasticity-robust SE, dev window only; NFCI enters with its existing 6-day publication lag. (4) Report the number of announcement days (~290 on dev) and, separately, the number of distinct NFCI-tight announcement days, since that is the real sample for the interaction. (5) Cost check: ~24 round trips a year at the existing ES/MNQ costs is roughly 15-40bp/yr of drag — small enough that the premium does not need to be large, which is the main practical attraction. (6) Pre-declared pass criterion: interaction t > 2.5 on ES with the same sign on MNQ, AND the base premium b positive. If b is positive but d is not, the honest conclusion is that the Savor-Wilson premium exists but is not state-dependent, which is a null for THIS hypothesis and must be reported as such rather than harvested as a base-effect finding.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: The repo tested (i) NFP-day holds unconditionally, which failed, and (ii) pre-FOMC drift, which failed its holdout. Neither is this. Neither pooled the three announcement types into the single event class the literature actually studies, and — the substantive difference — neither made the position SIGN OR SIZE a function of the macro state. The failed 735-test sweep asked 'does NFCI predict the next 20 days' and got ~0; this asks 'does NFCI predict how much you get paid on the 2 event days inside those 20', which is a different question with roughly 10x the signal-to-noise per unit of exposure and no overlap penalty.

hypotheses.name: JPY_CARRY_CROWDING_CONVEXITY (crowding predicts the TAIL, not the mean — a risk overlay, not a signal)
hypotheses.claim: Carry crowding has no predictive power for the MEAN return of USDJPY — which is exactly what the repo's dead FX-carry test found — but it has strong predictive power for the LEFT TAIL. Define a crowding index at each weekly COT release: C = z_104w(net-noncommercial JPY short / OI) + z_252d(6-month USDJPY return) − z_252d(60-day realised USDJPY volatility). CLAIM: P(the maximum drawdown of a long-USDJPY position over the following 20 trading days exceeds 3%) is increasing and CONVEX in C, with a sharp break in the top decile — the top-decile hazard is more than double the unconditional hazard — while E[20-day return | C] is flat across all deciles. Practical form: gating out top-decile-C weeks improves the Calmar ratio of the existing USDJPY trend leg without materially reducing its return.
hypotheses.mechanism: Carry is short volatility with a mechanical unwind. The position is levered and funded, so the constraint that matters is margin, not opinion. Positions accumulate slowly while spot grinds in the carry direction and realised vol falls — falling vol mechanically permits MORE leverage per unit of risk budget, which is why low vol is part of the crowding index rather than a comfort signal. When a shock arrives, every holder faces a margin call simultaneously against a position that has become large relative to available liquidity, and the unwind is a jump rather than a drift: 'up the stairs, down the elevator' is not a metaphor here, it is the documented shape of the carry return distribution (Brunnermeier-Nagel-Pedersen 2008 on carry crash risk and its link to funding liquidity). The critical point for THIS repo: this mechanism predicts a change in SKEW and in tail probability, and is almost silent about the conditional mean — so every mean-return test run so far, including the dead FX carry test, was testing the one moment the theory does not speak to.
hypotheses.data_needed: All on disk. COT: JAPANESE YEN - CHICAGO MERCANTILE EXCHANGE is present in the deacot zips (verified). Prices: data/daily/USDJPY.csv. Realised vol computed from the same. The existing USDJPY trend leg from run_breadth.py provides the overlay test bed, with its declared cost of 0.0125.
hypotheses.how_to_test: 3 pre-declared tests. (1) Build C weekly with the existing COT timing (as-of Tuesday, tradeable from the following Monday) and the 252-day trailing z-scores on price-based components; no component uses future data. (2) TAIL TEST: logistic regression of the binary outcome 1[min cumulative 20-day return < −3%] on C, plus a decile table of the realised hazard rate. The convexity claim is tested by comparing the fit of a linear-in-C logit against one with a top-decile dummy — a likelihood-ratio test with one degree of freedom, pre-declared as the convexity test. Note the 20-day outcome windows overlap, so inference must be by block-bootstrap (block length 20 weeks) rather than an analytic logit SE, which would be badly overstated. (3) MEAN TEST, and it is pre-declared as a NULL I expect to confirm: E[20d return | C decile] should show no monotone pattern. If the mean test comes out significant it is more likely to be a sign that C is proxying trend than a sign that the hypothesis is right — I will treat a significant mean as a red flag, not a win. (4) OVERLAY TEST, the only tradeable claim: apply the gate (flat when C is in its top decile, using a threshold estimated on a trailing expanding window so the decile boundary is never estimated with future data) to the existing dev USDJPY trend leg; compare Calmar and max drawdown, with the DIFFERENCE in Sharpe bootstrapped rather than eyeballed. Dev only. (5) Honest caveat I will state before running: 2010-2022 contains only a handful of genuine yen-carry unwinds (2011 Tohoku, 2013, 2016, 2020), so even the tail test rests on perhaps 6-10 independent stress episodes. If the top-decile hazard is not at least double the base rate, this is not worth pursuing — a subtle effect on 8 episodes is indistinguishable from luck.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: The dead tests were 'FX carry' (a linear carry-differential signal) and 'US-JP carry differential' within the 735-test sweep — both mean-return tests on the interest-rate differential, and both using conditional-mean machinery (Spearman IC, tertiles, sign(z)). Positioning-based crowding for JPY has never been built (COT work covered GOLD, EUR, NQ, then 9 markets, always via the same net-position z-score and always testing the mean). And no test in this repo has EVER targeted a moment other than the mean: every result in research/ is a mean return, a Sharpe, or a t-stat on a mean. A conditional-tail-probability model is a genuinely different object and, if it works, plugs into the existing book as a risk overlay rather than as another correlated return leg.

hypotheses.name: DURATION_DIFFERENTIAL_CONVEXITY (Nasdaq-minus-S&P responds to rate shocks only above a threshold)
hypotheses.claim: Real-yield shocks have no reliable predictive relationship with the LEVEL of either equity index — confirmed by the sweep — but they do have one with the SPREAD between them, and only for large shocks. CLAIM: let Δry be the 2-day change in the 10y TIPS real yield (DFII10, publication-lagged), and let R = the vol-normalised 5-day forward return of ES minus that of MNQ. The sensitivity of R to Δry is approximately zero for small shocks and strongly positive for large ones: R = a + b·Δry + c·Δry·1[|Δry| > q90] + e, where q90 is the 90th percentile of |Δry| over a trailing 3-year window, and the hypothesis is that c > 0 and dominates b. In words: after a LARGE real-yield rise, long ES / short MNQ over the following week; after a large fall, the reverse; after small moves, do nothing.
hypotheses.mechanism: The Nasdaq is longer-duration equity — more of its value sits in distant cash flows — so its discount-rate sensitivity is genuinely higher than the S&P's. That is an identity, not a hypothesis. The hypothesis is about WHY the differential is predictable rather than instantaneous, and about why it is convex. Convexity: for small rate moves, the cross-sectional dispersion in earnings news swamps the duration effect, so the differential response is buried in noise and is not even reliably signed. Only when the rate move is large enough to dominate idiosyncratic news does duration become the organising factor for relative pricing. Predictability: the adjustment mechanism is a reallocation of capital between growth and value mandates — fund flows, model portfolio rebalances, factor-book risk reductions — and that capital is slow-moving, taking days rather than seconds to move (the standard slow-moving-capital argument, Duffie 2010). The instantaneous index-level response is arbitraged; the style-rotation flow it triggers is not.
hypotheses.data_needed: All on disk: data/daily/ES.csv, data/daily/MNQ.csv, data/external/macro/DFII10.csv (PUB_LAG 1 day, so a 2-day change through t−1 is known at t and the position is taken at the t open). Costs for both legs already declared in run_shorter.COST (ES 0.62, MNQ 1.62 price points).
hypotheses.how_to_test: ONE regression with a pre-declared threshold, 2 tests (the interaction coefficient, and the tradeable leg). (1) Compute R as a dollar-vol-matched spread — each leg scaled by its own trailing 60-day vol so the spread is beta-neutral by construction rather than by estimation, and so the result cannot be a disguised directional equity bet. (2) MANDATORY DE-CONFOUNDING, declared first: 2010-2021 is a period of secularly falling real yields AND secular Nasdaq outperformance, so a naive regression will find the 'right' answer for entirely spurious reasons. The intercept a absorbs the secular drift, and I additionally require the result to hold with the sample de-meaned within each calendar year — if the effect disappears once the secular trend is removed, it was the trend. (3) The threshold q90 is computed on a TRAILING 3-year window, never in-sample, and is not tuned; 90th percentile is fixed in advance. (4) t deflated by sqrt(5) for the 5-day overlap, Newey-West with 5 lags, plus an episode-level check on non-overlapping large-shock events (expect roughly 60-100 on dev — this is one of the better-powered proposals here precisely because rate shocks are frequent, unlike credit or liquidity episodes). (5) Cost is the main practical risk and must be applied honestly: this is a two-legged trade, so the round-trip cost is roughly double a single-instrument leg. The repo has already killed one spread trade (gold/silver) on exactly this. Pre-declared pass criterion: the interaction survives AND the net-of-cost spread Sharpe on dev exceeds 0.5 — a gross-only result should be recorded as a failure, since the gold/silver ratio also looked fine gross.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: The sweep tested real_yield and real_yield_chg4w against each of 7 markets SEPARATELY. A common factor that moves ES and MNQ in the same direction cancels out of every one of those tests as noise while being precisely the signal here — testing a difference is not the same test as testing two levels, and no relative-value equity-index specification appears anywhere in the repo. The convex threshold is the second departure: the sweep's tertile split on real_yield_chg4w pools a large negative shock with a mildly negative one, which under this hypothesis is exactly the wrong aggregation. Distinct from the gold/silver pair test in instrument, mechanism (duration vs a stable ratio), and cost profile (index futures, not CFD metals).

result.lens:
JAPAN AND THE CARRY TRADE — grounded in a data audit of the repo, not speculation.

WHAT I VERIFIED (all free, no API key, fetched successfully during this session):
1. MoF daily JGB yield curve — https://www.mof.go.jp/english/policy/jgbs/reference/interest_rate/historical/jgbcme_all.csv (HTTP 200, 1.19MB). Columns 1Y..40Y, daily. 10Y: 9,929 obs 1986-07-05 -> 2026-08-31; 4,076 rows since 2010. This matters enormously: qlab/macro.py's carry_us_jp uses IRLTLT01JPM156N, which is MONTHLY OECD data carrying PUB_LAG 45. So the "US-JP carry differential" inside the 735 tests was a 45-day-stale monthly number. Every JGB hypothesis below is therefore NOT a re-run of that test at all — it is the first daily-resolution look. Published after the Tokyo close (~02:00-03:00 ET), so day T is safely usable for a T+1 decision (lag 1, same convention as DGS10).
2. MoF weekly Japanese portfolio flows — https://www.mof.go.jp/policy/international_policy/reference/itn_transactions_in_securities/week.csv (HTTP 200). Shift-JIS, 1,130 weekly rows from 2005-01-02 to 2026-08-29. Splits acquisition/disposal/NET across Equity, Long-term debt, Short-term debt, for BOTH Portfolio Investment Assets (Japanese buying foreign) and Liabilities (foreigners buying Japanese). Nothing in this repo has ever touched Japanese flow data. ~650 weekly obs in a 2010-2022 dev window.
3. BOJ decision dates are scrapeable per year (boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/mpr_YYYY/index.htm, HTTP 200, dates in <td> cells).

WHAT I MEASURED ON DEV DATA (n=3,604 daily, <2022-07-01), which shaped the proposals:
- lag-1 corr(USDJPY ret, MNQ ret) = -0.028; lag-1 corr(USDJPY, JPXJPY) = -0.020. Directional carry spillover at daily frequency is DEAD, exactly as the 735-test result predicts. I therefore propose ZERO directional lagged-carry hypotheses.
- Contemporaneous corr(USDJPY, JPXJPY) = 0.505 — the Nikkei's yen-beta is large and real.
- Rolling-20d corr(USDJPY, MNQ): mean 0.23, sd 0.33, p10 -0.23, p90 +0.64. The correlation REGIME is a genuinely dispersed, non-degenerate state variable even though the level carries no directional signal. That asymmetry is the single most interesting thing I found and drives H2.

WHAT I REJECTED RATHER THAN PAD THE LIST (ruthlessness, as asked):
- MoF FX intervention reaction function: only ~4 episodes before 2022-07-01 (2010-09, 2011-03, 2011-08, 2011-10). All the 2022/2024 interventions are in holdout. Dead on arrival; also needs unstructured news text for the verbal-escalation ladder.
- Japanese fiscal-year-end (Mar 31) repatriation and Golden Week: 12 observations in the dev window. Not worth a slot, and it is the same family as the already-dead turn-of-month.
- GPIF rebalancing: quarterly disclosure, ~50 dev obs, and the flow is not dated precisely enough to trade.
- BOJ announcement-time "lateness" (late release = contentious = policy change) — a real Tokyo-desk regularity, but BOJ does not publish historical release timestamps in any structured form. Fails the free-and-obtainable bar.
- Pre-BOJ meeting drift: same family as pre-FOMC drift, which already failed holdout. Not re-proposing a known-dead shape.
