- YCC band-pressure / curve-pinning distortion: mechanically elegant and computable from the MoF curve as a 10Y fitting residual against 9Y/15Y, but YCC ended in 2024, so even a positive result has no forward tradability. Cut on those grounds.
- stooq JGB CSVs are now behind a JavaScript proof-of-work challenge; not scriptable. FRED has no daily JGB. MoF is the only free daily source.

DESIGN PRINCIPLE ACROSS ALL SIX: the 0-of-735 result is decisive evidence against "lagged macro level/change -> directional mean return, linear, unconditional." The carry trade's defining empirical property is not a predictable mean — it is negative skew with time-varying, crowding-dependent CRASH risk. So four of the six below target conditional tails, second moments, regimes, or hedged relative value rather than the unconditional mean, and each pre-registers a SMALL number of tests (3-8, stated explicitly) so the FDR denominator stays honest. Priors are set against this repo's brutal base rate: roughly one survivor in over a thousand tests. Nothing here deserves a prior above 0.2.

hypotheses.name: CARRY_CRASH_TAIL — crowding x funding-repricing predicts the LEFT TAIL of the yen, not its mean
hypotheses.claim: A pre-registered carry-stress state S_t, built from (a) CFTC JPY non-commercial net-short/OI z-scored over 104 weeks, (b) the 20-day change in the MoF daily JGB 2Y yield, and (c) USDJPY's stretch above its 200d MA, does NOT shift the mean of forward 10-day USDJPY returns, but DOES shift the left tail: in the top quintile of S_t the 5th-percentile and CVaR(5%) of forward 10d USDJPY returns are materially worse (I predict >=1.5x the unconditional left-tail magnitude), and the same state raises left-tail severity for MNQ/ES. The tradeable form is not a directional signal but a de-risking overlay.
hypotheses.mechanism: Yen-funded carry positions are levered and financed short. Their return distribution is small-positive-most-weeks, large-negative-rarely, because unwinding is triggered by VaR and margin systems rather than by views. Crowding (COT net short) measures how much levered position must be liquidated; a rise in the JGB 2Y raises the funding cost that motivates liquidation; stretch measures how far the position is from fair value. None of these three needs to predict the mean for all three to predict the severity of the liquidation when it comes. This is the Brunnermeier-Nagel-Pedersen crash-risk result, and it is a statement about the third and fifth percentiles, not the first moment — which is precisely why 735 mean-regressions could find nothing while this could still be true.
hypotheses.data_needed: On disk: data/external/cot/deacot*.zip (CFTC, 1999-2026; the 'JAPANESE YEN - CHICAGO MERCANTILE EXCHANGE' contract is already parsed in run_cot_breadth.py), data/daily/USDJPY.csv, MNQ.csv, ES.csv. Fetch once: MoF daily JGB curve, https://www.mof.go.jp/english/policy/jgbs/reference/interest_rate/historical/jgbcme_all.csv (verified HTTP 200 this session; skiprows=1, Date as %Y/%m/%d, '-' means missing).
hypotheses.how_to_test: Dev window only (<2022-07-01). Timing: COT is as-of Tuesday, released Friday 15:30 ET, so the z-score applies from the FOLLOWING MONDAY (+6 calendar days) — the convention already used in run_cot.py. JGB 2Y from MoF gets lag 1 (published after the Tokyo close). S_t = mean of the three cross-sectionally standardised components, recomputed only with data available at t. Then: (1) quantile regression of forward 10d USDJPY return on S_t at tau = 0.05, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.95 — the pre-registered prediction is a significant NEGATIVE slope at tau=0.05 and an INSIGNIFICANT slope at tau=0.50. A significant slope at the median would falsify the specific mechanism (it would just be the already-dead directional claim). (2) Two-sample comparison of CVaR(5%) between top-quintile S_t and the rest, with a stationary block bootstrap (block ~20d) for the p-value, since forward 10d returns overlap. Report the t-stat at the signal's native WEEKLY frequency and deflate any overlapping-return t by sqrt(10). (3) Repeat the CVaR test for MNQ and ES as the spillover leg. That is 5 quantile slopes + 3 CVaR tests = 8 pre-registered tests; apply Benjamini-Hochberg across all 8 and against the standing repo family. Economic evaluation: apply S_t as a leverage multiplier (1.0 normally, 0.5 in the top quintile) on the surviving MNQ daily-momentum leg and check whether max drawdown and Calmar improve while Sharpe is not degraded — costs at the repo's USDJPY 0.025 / MNQ 1.62 round-trip. Falsification is explicit: if the tau=0.50 slope is significant and tau=0.05 is not, the hypothesis is wrong in the way that matters.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: run_cot.py and run_cot_breadth.py already tested JPY COT positioning, but only as a CONTRARIAN MEAN signal on USDJPY at a weekly horizon (z<-1.5 washout). That is a first-moment claim. This is a conditional-tail claim, adds a daily JGB funding-cost term the repo has never had at daily resolution, and is evaluated cross-asset as a risk overlay rather than as a directional FX trade. The 735 macro tests were all linear mean regressions and included no quantile or CVaR test at all.

hypotheses.name: JPY_LEVERAGE_REGIME — the yen-equity correlation is a leverage-intermediation regime, not a signal
hypotheses.claim: The trailing 20-day correlation between USDJPY and MNQ returns, rho_t, is a state variable that conditions the performance of trend/momentum, even though USDJPY returns themselves have no lagged directional information. Specifically: when rho_t is high (top tercile, roughly >+0.45 on dev data), global leverage is being intermediated through the yen, subsequent equity drawdowns are deeper and daily momentum underperforms; when rho_t is near zero the yen is driven by domestic Japanese factors and momentum performs normally. Predicted effect: conditional Sharpe of the MNQ daily-momentum leg is materially lower in the high-rho tercile, and conditional 20d max drawdown is materially larger.
hypotheses.mechanism: The yen is the world's funding currency. When a common leverage factor is driving both risk assets and the funding leg, USDJPY and equities co-move — that is the observable signature of levered carry being on. In that state, positions across unrelated assets are held by the same balance sheets, so a shock propagates as forced correlated selling and trends break abruptly. When the yen decouples (BOJ-specific news, domestic flows), that shared-balance-sheet channel is quiet. Crucially this predicts second moments and strategy conditional performance, not returns — consistent with the observed lag-1 corr of -0.028 that kills the directional version.
hypotheses.data_needed: Entirely on disk: data/daily/USDJPY.csv, MNQ.csv, ES.csv, JPXJPY.csv. No fetch required, zero data cost.
hypotheses.how_to_test: Dev window only. rho_t uses returns through t-1 only, so it is causal by construction; no publication lag applies since both legs are prices. Pre-register exactly 4 tests: (1) regress the MNQ daily-momentum leg's daily PnL on a high-rho dummy, Newey-West t with 20 lags; (2) same for the ES leg; (3) compare conditional 20d max drawdown across terciles via block bootstrap; (4) verify the gate is not a VIX proxy in disguise — regress the momentum PnL on the high-rho dummy AFTER controlling for the VIX tercile, and require the rho coefficient to survive. Test 4 is the one that matters: if rho is merely restating VIX, the hypothesis is dead, because VIX-based gating already failed here. Then apply as a binary leverage gate (full size / half size), costs at MNQ 1.62 round-trip, and compute a DEFLATED Sharpe that charges for the fact that the ungated leg was already selected. Report BH across the 4 tests plus the standing family. IMPORTANT HONEST COST: this hypothesis touches the ONE strategy that survived, so a positive dev result must be confirmed on holdout, and that spends holdout on the single asset the programme cannot afford to overfit. I would only run this after the other five, and only if the dev effect is large enough to be worth the holdout burn.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: VIX term-structure gating and volume gating both failed, so the gating family has a poor record here — that is priced into the low prior. But those gates measured market-wide fear and participation; this measures whether the funding leg is co-moving, which is a different economic object, and test 4 is designed specifically to prove it is not a VIX restatement. The 735 tests used USDJPY only through the monthly, 45-day-lagged carry_us_jp feature and never constructed a conditional correlation at all. Measured dev dispersion (sd 0.33, p10 -0.23, p90 +0.64) confirms the state variable is not degenerate.

hypotheses.name: JP_WEEKLY_FLOWS — MoF weekly Japanese portfolio flows as the direct measurement of the repatriation channel
hypotheses.claim: Weekly net purchases of foreign long-term debt securities by Japanese residents (MoF Portfolio Investment Assets, long-term debt, NET), z-scored over 104 weeks, predicts next-week USDJPY: heavy net BUYING of foreign bonds (yen sold to fund it) precedes further yen weakness, and sharp net SELLING (repatriation) precedes yen strength. Predicted weekly IC in the 0.06-0.10 range, and stronger in the tails (|z|>1.5) than in the middle.
hypotheses.mechanism: This is not a proxy for the carry/repatriation channel — it IS the channel, measured directly. Japanese lifers, banks and pension funds are among the world's largest cross-border bond buyers; when they buy foreign bonds unhedged they must sell yen, and when they repatriate they must buy it. Unlike every macro series in the failed 735 (which are prices or aggregates that markets already discount), this is a quantity: actual settled transaction volume by the specific investor base whose behaviour defines the carry trade. Flow data has a different information structure from price data — it reveals who did what, and institutional flows are persistent because mandates and hedging programmes change slowly, which is what makes the autocorrelated component potentially predictive.
hypotheses.data_needed: Fetch once: https://www.mof.go.jp/policy/international_policy/reference/itn_transactions_in_securities/week.csv (verified HTTP 200 this session; Shift-JIS encoding, English column labels on row 12, 1,130 weekly rows from 2005-01-02 to 2026-08-29, unit = 100 million yen, thousands separators and trailing spaces inside quoted fields need stripping). Plus data/daily/USDJPY.csv and JPXJPY.csv on disk.
hypotheses.how_to_test: Dev window only. Publication lag is the crux and must be conservative: MoF publishes the weekly report on the THURSDAY following the reference week (which ends Saturday). Set the position to apply from the following FRIDAY's close, i.e. week-ending-Saturday + 6 calendar days — never earlier, and verify the lag empirically by checking the 'Final Update' date stamped in the file header against the last reference week. Pre-register exactly 6 tests: Spearman IC of z(net foreign long-term debt purchases) against next-week USDJPY return; same for the equity-assets leg; same for the Liabilities side (foreigners buying Japanese equity) against next-week JPXJPY; and the three tail versions (|z|>1.5 vs middle, Welch t). Native frequency is WEEKLY so t-stats are computed on ~650 non-overlapping weekly observations with no sqrt(h) deflation needed. Costs at USDJPY 0.025 round-trip on a weekly rebalance. BH across the 6 plus the standing family. Sanity check first: confirm the series is not simply a lagged transform of USDJPY itself by checking the contemporaneous correlation — if flows are just mechanically restating the FX move, there is nothing here.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: No Japanese flow data of any kind exists in this repo — the macro directory holds 31 FRED series, none of them Japanese portfolio flows, and the only Japan inputs are monthly JGB yields, monthly BOJ assets and DEXJPUS. This is a genuinely new dataset measuring a quantity rather than a price. The counter-argument, which is why the prior stays low: this release is watched closely by every macro desk in Tokyo every Thursday, so the obvious component is likely already in price by Friday's open.

hypotheses.name: UNWIND_CASCADE — funding-currency tail moves continue for days; ordinary-currency tail moves do not
hypotheses.claim: Conditional on a large single-day yen appreciation (USDJPY return < -1.5%, roughly the 1st-2nd percentile), the following 2-5 days show significant NEGATIVE continuation in USDJPY, whereas large yen DEPRECIATION days show no comparable continuation. The asymmetry is the claim. The falsifying control is EURUSD: the euro is not a primary funding currency, so the same test on EURUSD should show no such asymmetry. If EURUSD shows the same effect, the hypothesis is generic FX tail behaviour and is rejected.
hypotheses.mechanism: Forced deleveraging is a multi-day process, not an instantaneous one. Margin and VaR systems recalculate on a daily cycle: a large adverse move on day T raises measured risk, which triggers position cuts that execute on T+1 and T+2, which moves price further, which triggers the next round. That mechanical cascade is specific to the direction in which the position is levered — carry is structurally SHORT yen, so only yen APPRECIATION forces the cascade. Yen depreciation makes existing carry positions profitable and forces nobody. This directional asymmetry has no counterpart in a non-funding currency, which is exactly what the EURUSD control tests. August 2024 is the canonical example; the dev window contains the 2013, 2015-08 and 2016-01/02 analogues, plus 2020-03.
hypotheses.data_needed: Entirely on disk: data/daily/USDJPY.csv, data/daily/EURUSD.csv (both 2010-01-03 onward, verified). Optionally data/USDJPY_15m.csv to check whether the continuation is concentrated in the Tokyo session. Zero fetch cost.
hypotheses.how_to_test: Dev window only. Pre-register exactly 6 tests: mean forward 2d, 3d and 5d USDJPY return after a < -1.5% day (3 tests), and the mirror set after a > +1.5% day (3 tests), each versus the unconditional mean, Welch t with a stationary block bootstrap because event windows overlap; deflate the overlapping-return t by sqrt(h). Then run the identical 6 on EURUSD as a control and require the yen asymmetry to be significantly larger than the euro asymmetry (difference-in-differences on the two asymmetry statistics). Report the event count explicitly — I expect only 30-60 qualifying days in the dev window, so this is genuinely underpowered and a null result will be uninformative rather than disconfirming; say so in the writeup rather than reading a null as evidence of absence. Costs at USDJPY 0.025 round-trip, which is material relative to a 3-day hold. BH across 12 tests plus the standing family. Threshold sensitivity must be reported at -1.0%, -1.5% and -2.0% but only -1.5% counts as the pre-registered test; the other two are shown to demonstrate the result is not knife-edge.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: The 122 candlestick tests and the ML-on-price work searched for patterns in a symmetric, unconditional way across all markets; none of them posed a directional-asymmetry hypothesis tied to a named funding mechanism, and none used a matched control asset to separate an asset-specific mechanism from generic behaviour. The control design is what makes this worth running: it can distinguish 'yen carry unwind' from 'FX tails cluster', which no test in the repo has attempted. Pure price signals do have a poor record here, which is why the prior stays near the repo base rate.

hypotheses.name: JGB_VOL_SPILLOVER — Japanese rate volatility as incremental information for global equity volatility
hypotheses.claim: Realised volatility of the daily MoF JGB 10Y yield adds statistically significant incremental explanatory power to a HAR-RV forecast of MNQ and ES realised volatility at 5- and 20-day horizons, over and above own realised volatility and VIX. Predicted: a positive, significant coefficient on the JGB-RV term with Newey-West t > 2.5 after controlling for both, and an out-of-sample QLIKE improvement over the HAR+VIX baseline.
hypotheses.mechanism: JGBs are the collateral base of the world's largest creditor nation and the reference rate for the cheapest funding in the system. When JGB yields become volatile, the value of the collateral against which yen funding is extended becomes uncertain, hedging costs on the several trillion dollars of FX-hedged foreign bonds held by Japanese institutions reprice, and the volatility of the funding leg propagates into the volatility of everything financed by it. Volatility, unlike direction, is genuinely forecastable — this is the one place in the macro landscape where the base rate is favourable — and the honest payoff is better vol targeting and drawdown control on the surviving strategy, not alpha.
hypotheses.data_needed: Fetch once: the MoF daily JGB curve CSV (verified above; use the 10Y column, 4,076 rows since 2010). On disk: data/daily/MNQ.csv, ES.csv, and data/external/macro/VIXCLS.csv.
hypotheses.how_to_test: Dev window only. JGB 10Y gets lag 1 (MoF publishes after the Tokyo close, so day T is usable for a T+1 decision); VIXCLS already carries PUB_LAG 1 in qlab/macro.py. Build JGB-RV as the 20d standard deviation of daily JGB 10Y yield CHANGES in basis points, not of the level. Baseline: HAR-RV on the target (daily, weekly, monthly RV terms) plus contemporaneous-available VIX. Treatment: baseline + JGB-RV. Pre-register exactly 4 tests: the JGB-RV coefficient t-stat for MNQ and for ES, at 5d and 20d horizons, Newey-West with lags = horizon, and the overlapping-regression t deflated by sqrt(h). Out-of-sample check by expanding-window QLIKE and MSE against the baseline. BH across the 4 plus the standing family. CRITICAL CAVEAT to state up front: from 2016 to 2022 the BOJ pinned the 10Y under YCC, so JGB-RV is near-flat over roughly half the dev window and almost all the interesting variation (2022-2024) sits in holdout. The usable dev variation is concentrated in 2010-2016, which includes the April-May 2013 JGB VaR shock and 2015. Report the dev sub-sample sizes honestly and treat a 2016-2022 null as uninformative rather than as evidence against.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: Every one of the 735 tests targeted RETURNS; not one targeted volatility. The repo has no HAR-RV model at all, and VIX has only ever been used as a return predictor or as a gate on an existing signal, never as a baseline to beat in a volatility forecast. Daily JGB yields have never existed in this repo — the only Japanese rate series on disk is monthly with a 45-day lag, which cannot produce a realised-volatility measure at all.

hypotheses.name: HEDGED_PICKUP — the FX-hedged yield advantage of foreign bonds to a Japanese investor, as a relative-duration signal
hypotheses.claim: Define hedged_pickup = (US10Y - US3M) - (JGB10Y - JGB1Y), the difference in curve slopes, which to first order is the yield a Japanese investor earns on a currency-hedged foreign bond over a domestic one. When hedged_pickup falls toward or below zero, the marginal Japanese buyer stays home, global term premia rise, and LONG-DURATION assets underperform SHORT-DURATION ones. Tested as a relative claim only: TLT vs IEF, and XLK vs XLU, over 20-60 day horizons. Predicted: a positive, significant slope of hedged_pickup on the forward long-minus-short duration spread return.
hypotheses.mechanism: For a hedged bond investor the FX hedge cost is approximately the short-rate differential, so the hedged pickup is not the 10Y differential (the already-tested carry) but the difference of the two curve SLOPES — a distinct functional form. Japan is the world's largest net creditor and its institutions are the marginal price-insensitive buyer of global duration; when the hedged pickup vanishes, that bid withdraws and duration risk premia must rise to clear. Expressing it as a relative-value spread rather than a directional bet is deliberate: the 735 tests established that macro cannot predict the equity or bond beta, so the spread strips out the component that is demonstrably unpredictable and isolates the relative-duration component that the mechanism actually speaks to.
hypotheses.data_needed: Fetch once: MoF daily JGB curve (10Y and 1Y columns; note the curve has no tenor below 1Y, so JGB1Y is the short-rate proxy — an approximation that must be stated, not hidden). On disk: data/external/macro/DGS10.csv, data/external/DTB3.csv (daily, verified through 2026-09-03), data/external/etf_TLT_1d.csv, etf_IEF_1d.csv, etf_XLK_1d.csv, etf_XLU_1d.csv (all daily from 2009).
hypotheses.how_to_test: Dev window only. Lags: DGS10 and DTB3 lag 1 per PUB_LAG convention; JGB legs lag 1. Pre-register exactly 4 tests: regress the forward 20d and 60d TLT-minus-IEF return, and the forward 20d and 60d XLK-minus-XLU return, on the level of hedged_pickup. Newey-West t with lags = horizon, then deflate by sqrt(h) for the overlap. Costs charged on both legs of the spread at ETF round-trip levels. BH across the 4 plus the standing family. Two mandatory sanity checks before believing anything: (1) confirm hedged_pickup is not merely a relabelled US curve slope — regress it on T10Y3M and require the JGB component to carry independent variation, otherwise this collapses into the already-dead 3m10y test; (2) confirm the sign of the effect is stable across the 2010-2016 and 2016-2022 sub-periods, since the JGB slope was heavily distorted by YCC in the latter. This is the weakest of the six because it is closest in shape to the family that produced 0-of-735, and the prior reflects that.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_tested: The 735 included curve 2s10s, 3m10y, term premium and 'US-JP carry differential' — but that last one was the raw 10Y level difference built from a MONTHLY series with a 45-day lag, and none of them was a difference of SLOPES, which is the actual hedged-investor quantity. The dependent variable is also different in kind: every one of the 735 predicted an outright market return, whereas this predicts a market-neutral duration spread. Sanity check (1) is included precisely to kill it fast if it turns out to be the US curve slope wearing a costume.
